text:
Ashley (Support): Hey team — Velara reported a spike of 429s and tail latency going >1.2s since yesterday 09:00 UTC. They've got a dedicated pool velara-prod-1. Can we confirm current pool sizing and autoscale behavior? They expect baseline ~120 QPS, peak 900 QPS for marketing bursts. Logs show many 429s during 800-900 QPS window.

Eva (Customer Success): Noted. Velara on annual reserved plan, SLA 99.9. They're seeing customer-facing errors. I told them we're triaging. Please treat as P2.

Marcus (SRE): Pulling metrics now. pool_id=velara-prod-1. Observing sustained 75% utilization at baseline and spikes to 98% during bursts. Autoscale policy 'p90-step' didn't kick in until queue growth went >300 reqs. Suspect warmup / cold-starts of worker pods.

Li (Eng-Platform): Can you paste the pool config? I'm interested in min_replicas, max_replicas, scale_cpu_threshold, and cooldown windows.

Ashley (Support): Config snippet from prod console:
```
pool: velara-prod-1
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 10
scale_cpu_threshold: 70%
scale_cooldown_sec: 120
burst_mode: enabled
```

Marcus (SRE): That explains the gap. With min 2 and slow cooldown, bursts from 120->900 QPS overwhelm initial capacity. Also no pre-warm. Suggest increasing min_replicas to 4 and set burst_headroom to 40% and enable predictive warmup.

Li (Eng-Platform): Agree. Also want to check per-tenant concurrency limits and routing policy — if multiple customers share nodes it's noisy neighbor. What's the node oversubscription factor? Marcus, can you share container-level cpu/mem usage and queue lengths? Add the tracing correlation ids if possible.

Marcus (SRE): Attaching quick metrics paste:
- baseline 120 QPS -> tokens/sec ~14k -> GPU utilization ~52%
- bursts 820-920 QPS -> tokens/sec ~98k -> GPU utilization ~96-99%
- avg latency 210ms baseline -> 1.2s tail during burst
- auth failure rate -> 0.6% (minor) but 429 rate -> 8.3% during peak
Noisy neighbor observed: tenant 'gamma-inc' has sustained background jobs causing 30% shared GPU cycles.

Samir (Account): Velara is planning a marketing campaign next month with predicted ramp to 1200 QPS short bursts. Need recommended committed slab to avoid repeat outages.

Li (Eng-Platform): Proposed changes:
1) min_replicas: 6
2) max_replicas: 20
3) predictive_warmup: enabled with 3-min lookahead
4) burst_headroom: 50%
5) tenant isolation: move Velara to dedicated nodepool or enforce soft cpu shares for gamma-inc
Estimate cost delta: ~+22% monthly. Will produce a config PR and run canary.

Eva (Customer Success): I'll propose the dedicated nodepool option to Velara; they prefer reliability over cost. Samir can confirm if they want to trade cost.

Ashley (Support): Repro checklist for oncall:
- run curl load test against velara-prod endpoint simulating 900-1200 QPS for 5m
- monitor queue growth and 429 rate
- snapshot autoscale events and pod start latencies
- if 429s occur, run `kubectl logs` and capture kv-cache warm miss logs

Marcus (SRE): I'll run the repro in staging group now. Will share results in this thread. tagging @autoscale-bot for event dump.

autoscale-bot: Dump attached: events 1728001200-1728004200 (size 6MB) URL: https://internal/arb/events/velara-prod-1

Marcus (SRE): Staging run shows autoscale latency ~45s to add new replicas, cold-start GPU init ~18s, kv-cache rebuild ~25s. Combined ~88s before capacity alleviates 429s. Predictive warmup should cut that to <15s.

Li (Eng-Platform): I'll open infra PR to adjust policy and add tenant isolation flag. Marcus please include a small controlled canary and rollback plan.

Samir (Account): I'll email Velara with the proposed committed slab recommendation and estimated costs. Thanks team.

Ashley (Support): Thanks all. Keeping this thread open until post-deploy verification. Next update by EOD.
